subject: Panel data model with variable selection

messages.author: 6e0bce06355e4e6c
messages.subject: Panel data model with variable selection
parts:
Dear STAN users,

I am trying to estimate a panel-data model with AR2 errors:

for (i in 1:N){  #20 regions
 for (t in 1:T){  #35 years
  M[i,t] <- alpha[i] + inprod(beta1[]*X1[i,t,]) + inprod(beta2[],X2[i,t,])
  Err[i,t] <- Y[i,t] - M[i,t]
 }
 for (t in 3:T){
  Y[i,t] ~ normal( mu[i,t] , tau )
  mu[i,t] <- M[i,t] + rho[1]*Err[i,t-1] + rho[2]*Err[i,t-2]
}}  

This model is still a basic copy of the previous OpenBUGS implementation, which means that I have not yet looked at the best way to vectorize the code. Anyway, X1 contains a (relatively small) set of explanatory variables that are always included in the model specification, whereas X2 contains a large set of dummies of which only one or two are likely to be included. Hence the following prior is placed on beta2[]:

for (d in 1:30){
 ind2[d] ~ bernoulli(0.5) ;
 beta2[d] ~ normal( 0 , ind2[d]*100 + (1-ind2[d]) * 0.3 ); 
}

The values of mean=0 and stdev=0.3 are based on a prior runs of the model without variable selection, and allows for the sampling from a more informative prior when ind2 is 0. Also, for reporting purposes, the inference on ind2 (i.e. whether or not the X2 variables are included in the model specification) is more important than the estimated value of beta2[]. Is it possible to estimate this model using STAN - e.g. using the method described in chapter 9 of the manual? And perhaps someone has a suggestion on how to actually do this, if possible? Thank you!

Best regards,
Marcel Jonker

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Panel data model with variable selection
parts:
It looks a doable model in Stan.  One issue, which can be solved here, is that Stan does not support discrete sampling yet, so the following is problematic,

ind2[d] ~ bernoulli(0.5) ; 

But you can easily integrate out ind2 here and use a mixture for beta2.  Since you care more about ind2, you can get back to it when you have beta2.

--
Jiqiang

parts: > Also, do you already have an idea when STAN is going to include a slice sampler?

We plan to include slice sampling for discrete parameters.
It'll take a while before we get to it because it's not
at the top of our list of priorities (we're vectorizing
the existing code for speed first, then I'm working on
forward-mode auto-dif so we can do RM-HMC). Someone else
might be able to get to it, but I don't anticipate having
discrete sampling for at least six months.

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Panel data model with variable selection
parts:
I am not sure what is not clear for you.  First, apparently you have a mixture for beta2, whose pdf can be analytically written down and there are examples in the manual for how to sum up the log posterior for mixture of two (or more) components. 

Second, thought I do not think having ind2 is really important, but in each iteration, you can draw an ind2 given beta2, other parameters, and the data.  The forward sampling might not be done in Stan currently, but it can be easily carried out in, say R, after you complete the sampling. 

Regarding the slice sampler, I think for this problem you are still better off not using a discrete sampler as it is more efficient.

--
Jiqiang

Agreed. In all the problems with discrete parameters that
we've run into, they've been easy to marginalize out.
And that gives you better sampling efficiency and still allows
you to compute expectations with the results (or sample after
the fact).

The only cases we can imagine that have truly necessary integer
parameters are ones with missing data modeled as Poisson negative-binomial.

- Bob
